title: Angles: right, acute and obtuse
canonical_examples_source: Arithmetic self-verified; method ref: NCERT Class 5/6 Maths; format ref: bank uk-ks2-2024 maths.

blocks.content: An angle measures a turn or a corner. We sort angles into families by how big they are, measured in degrees.
A right angle is exactly 90 degrees — a square corner. An acute angle is smaller than 90 degrees.

steps: The corner of a book is a right angle: 90 degrees.
A narrow, sharp angle like 45 degrees is smaller than 90.
So 45 degrees is an acute angle.

blocks.explain: A right angle is a square corner, exactly 90 degrees.
blocks.rule: A right angle is exactly 90 degrees; an acute angle is less than 90 degrees.

an angle more than 90 degrees is called

blocks.content: An obtuse angle is bigger than 90 degrees but smaller than 180 degrees — a wide, open corner.

blocks.question: An angle of 45 degrees is:
blocks.explain: 45 is less than 90, so it is an acute angle.
blocks.rule: Acute is under 90 degrees, right is exactly 90, obtuse is over 90.

blocks.content: Under 90 is acute, exactly 90 is right, over 90 is obtuse. Compare every angle to the square corner. Let's practise!
